active_paradigms.idea: Optimal replication counts via water-filling binary search instead of greedy replicate_experts
active_paradigms.description: The current replicate_experts greedily picks the expert with max weight/logcnt, which is suboptimal. Instead, for each layer solve for replication counts directly: given R redundant experts, find integer counts c_i >= 1 with sum c_i = num_phy that minimizes max_i(w_i/c_i). This is solvable near-optimally: binary search on the target max load T, and for each T compute needed count ceil(w_i/T) per expert; find the smallest feasible T where sum ceil(w_i/T) <= num_phy, then distribute leftover replicas to experts with largest resulting w_i/c_i. This is a classic water-filling solution and is vectorized across all layers simultaneously with torch tensor ops (each binary search step is one tensor op over the whole batch). It typically achieves 5-15% lower max load than greedy and is O(log(max_w) * num_layers * num_log) — faster than the current O(num_redundant) sequential loop.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary load-balance score (min-max replica load) and algorithm runtime (replaces sequential replication loop with ~40 vectorized binary-search steps)
active_paradigms.cautions: After binary search, some experts may have count > 1 but leftover replicas must be assigned carefully: assign remaining replicas one at a time (or via a vectorized argmax of w_i/c_i) to keep feasibility. Ensure counts sum exactly to num_phy and every logical expert has at least 1 replica. Keep per-node decomposition from the hierarchical scheme.

active_paradigms.idea: Replace greedy LPT + limited swap refinement with Hungarian-style assignment refinement using scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment
active_paradigms.description: The balanced_packing greedy LPT followed by 16 heaviest/lightest swap iterations is a weak local search that only considers one pair of packs at a time. A stronger refinement: after greedy initialization, run repeated pairwise rebalancing where for the two most-loaded and least-loaded packs, solve the optimal reassignment of their combined 2*groups_per_pack items between the two packs exactly (this is a balanced partition problem solvable by sorting / subset selection), guaranteeing each pair is optimally split. Even better: for the final GPU packing step (Step 3), where each GPU gets exactly phy_experts_per_gpu items, formulate the refinement as a linear assignment problem: pick a candidate set of items and slots and use scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on a cost matrix designed to equalize loads (cost = |item_weight - target_slot_load|), iterating a few rounds. Since the evaluator runs single-threaded with torch threads=1, scipy on CPU is competitive and linear_sum_assignment is exact for each subproblem.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Load-balance quality (lower max and variance of pack loads at both node-packing and GPU-packing stages)
active_paradigms.cautions: scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment cost is O(n^3); keep the assignment subproblems small (only refine the top-k and bottom-k packs, e.g., k=4, or pairwise between extreme packs). Batch layers: process each layer's refinement independently but reuse the same code; the workload likely has modest layer counts so this stays within the 360s timeout. Must preserve the exact cardinality constraint (each pack keeps exactly groups_per_pack items) — use square cost matrices of size 2*groups_per_pack for pairwise refinement.

active_paradigms.idea: Global (non-hierarchical) rebalancing with multi-start perturbation and best-of-N selection
active_paradigms.description: The current algorithm always uses the hierarchical policy when num_groups % num_nodes == 0, forcing groups to stay node-local, which can be far from globally optimal when load is skewed across groups. Add a global policy path: treat all logical experts uniformly, compute replication counts via water-filling globally, then pack all physical experts to GPUs with balanced_packing, and compare the resulting objective (e.g., max per-GPU load or sum of squared loads) against the hierarchical result, returning whichever is better. Additionally, add a cheap multi-start: run the packing with a few deterministic perturbations of the sort order (e.g., rotate starting pack offsets, or jitter tie-breaking) and keep the best result by the evaluator-aligned objective computed locally. This is a portfolio approach: since scoring is deterministic, evaluating the true objective inside rebalance_experts and keeping the best of a handful of runs directly improves the score with only linear time cost.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary score via escaping the hierarchical policy's structural constraint; robustness across workload scenarios
active_paradigms.cautions: Must compute the local objective identically to the evaluator's notion of balance (check evaluator.py's metric — likely max GPU load or variance of per-GPU token counts including replica-count division). Keep total runtime bounded: 3-5 starts maximum, each fully vectorized. Ensure the global path still respects num_gpus divisibility and produces valid logical_to_physical_map with rank indices filling maxlogcnt slots correctly (scatter-based construction already handles this).

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace greedy LPT packing with Karmarkar-Karp differencing plus a min-max local search on GPU loads
tried_paradigms.description: The current balanced_packing uses greedy assignment then a narrow heaviest<->lightest swap loop. Instead, formulate the final GPU packing step as an explicit makespan minimization: first run the existing LPT to get an initial feasible solution, then run a vectorized local search that considers ALL (source GPU, dest GPU, expert) move/swap pairs per layer, accepting any move that strictly reduces max load (or sum of squares above the mean). Iterate until no improving move exists or a time budget (~2-3 seconds) is exhausted. This directly targets the max-GPU-load metric, which dominates the balance score, while keeping the vectorized numpy implementation fast enough for the runtime component of the score.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary balance score (max GPU load / mean load) with bounded runtime
tried_paradigms.cautions: Vectorize over layers with numpy; cap iterations by wall-clock time; ensure each pack still holds exactly num_phy/num_gpus experts; keep deterministic tie-breaking for reproducibility.
tried_paradigms.approach_type: numpy local search (custom vectorized min-max refinement)

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment for replica-to-GPU placement with cost matrix penalizing load imbalance
tried_paradigms.description: After replication counts are decided, the assignment of physical experts to GPUs is a structured assignment problem. Build a cost matrix per layer where entry (expert, gpu) encodes the resulting GPU load if this expert were placed there (e.g., current tentative load of gpu + expert weight), then solve a rectangular assignment (each expert to one slot, each slot capacity respected by expanding gpu columns into slot columns) with scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment. Repeat 3-5 rounds: each round recompute costs from the current loads and re-solve; this converges quickly to near-optimal min-max placements and replaces the heuristic packing entirely. Slots enforce the exact per-GPU expert-count constraint naturally via the expanded cost matrix.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Balance metric via globally optimal per-round assignment; runtime stays low since the assignment problem is solved exactly and quickly.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Expand GPUs into (gpu, slot) columns so cardinality constraints hold; handle the rectangular case (experts <= slots) that linear_sum_assignment supports; batch layers by solving each layer independently; use float64 costs scaled to avoid numerical issues.

tried_paradigms.idea: Binary-search the target max load and decide replication counts jointly with load, using a feasibility greedy
tried_paradigms.description: The current replicate_experts greedily replicates the highest load/copy expert, which is suboptimal because replication counts and placement interact. Instead, binary search a target per-GPU load T (between mean load and max load). For each T, decide replication counts so that ceil(w_i / T) replicas are allocated to each expert (capped by total physical budget, redistributing leftover replicas to the largest w_i/ceil(w_i/T) ratios), then check if all experts fit on GPUs under T using LPT with capacity T. This directly minimizes the theoretical lower bound on max load and produces replica counts matched to the achievable placement rather than chosen blindly. Use ~20 binary search iterations on a scalar, which is very fast.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Both the max-load lower bound (via optimal replication counts) and runtime (scalar binary search, vectorized feasibility check).
tried_paradigms.cautions: Handle the case where minimum total replicas (sum of ceil(w_i/T)) exceeds the physical budget: raise T accordingly; keep counts >= 1; ensure num_replicas total exactly; fall back to current greedy if the search fails.
tried_paradigms.approach_type: bisection on target load with capacity-driven replication (numpy)
